importance_ranking.reason: Tensile structures have extreme visual variation across shapes (conical, sail, hypar, umbrella, barrel vault), colours, and scale — buyers use the image to identify the product type and form factor before reading any text. Wrong shape or scale = immediate skip regardless of specs or price.

Fabric material (PVC vs PTFE vs HDPE) and GSM are primary shortlisting criteria — they define durability tier, service life, and price band. PVC and PTFE are non-interchangeable; a buyer cannot substitute one for the other without changing the project specification entirely.

Indian construction and fabrication buyers compare per-sq-ft rates aggressively across sellers once visual and material fit is confirmed. Price changes substantially with fabric material and GSM grade — PVC 850 GSM vs PTFE represents a 3–5x price difference — making price a primary shortlisting lever after spec confirmation.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Some sellers quote per sq metre (international fabric brands) or per project lump sum for large-span structures — this creates real price comparison confusion. Per sq ft is the dominant Indian market unit and must be shown alongside price to enable valid comparison.
importance_ranking.reason: Price cannot be compared without knowing the unit — per sq ft vs per sq metre vs per project lump sum are all present in the market and create genuine buyer confusion when unit is not displayed.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: Fabric brands (Serge Ferrari, Mehler, Sioen, SRF) are actively specified by architects and institutional buyers as quality and durability signals — a seller's fabric sourcing is a meaningful differentiator.
importance_ranking.reason: Institutional and commercial buyers evaluate completed project portfolio, fabric brand sourcing, and structural engineering capability during vendor selection — company credentials are a meaningful qualifier after initial shortlisting but not a primary scan signal.

top_configurator_specs.reason: PVC Coated, PTFE Coated, and HDPE are non-interchangeable product classes with 3–5x price differences and fundamentally different service life and application suitability — the single most important price-driving configurator.
Within the same material class, GSM (650–1050 GSM) defines the quality and durability tier with a meaningful price delta and determines structural compliance for wind load requirements.

missing_important_specs.why_important: The area to be covered (sq ft) drives structural design complexity, mast count, cable configuration, and total project cost — sellers cannot scope or price a project without this dimension.
Buyers in hospitality, residential, and commercial segments specify colour (white, grey, blue, custom) as a primary aesthetic requirement — colour selection affects fabric sourcing and pricing.

top_rfq_specs.reason: PVC Coated, PTFE, and PVDF are non-interchangeable material tiers with fundamentally different price points and durability profiles — sellers need this to determine which product line to quote and whether they can supply.
GSM grade within a material class defines the quality tier and drives per-sq-ft pricing — sellers need this to confirm they stock the required grade and to provide an accurate quote.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers need to know the intended application (car parking, entrance canopy, food court, sports court) to determine structural requirements, span, load design, and project scope before they can respond accurately.

The approximate area to be covered (sq ft) is the primary project scoping dimension — a 200 sq ft canopy and a 5000 sq ft food court cover require entirely different structural designs and cost structures.
